skills.name: Probability and sample spaces
skills.key: P(event) = favorable outcomes / total outcomes, always between 0 and 1. 0 = impossible, 1 = certain, 1/2 = equally likely either way.
tiers: list a sample space; classify likelihood (impossible..certain)
P of a simple event as a fraction, decimal, percent
P of 'not' an event; place on a 0-1 line
relative frequency from collected data -> predicted count
skills.gen: Spinners with 3-8 sectors, bags of 5-20 items in 2-4 colors, dice, cards labeled A-F. Never a probability above 1.

errors.desc: assumes outcomes are equally likely when they are not

skills.skin: dud missile odds, weather, radar contact chance, ordnance bag draws

skills.name: Experimental and theoretical probability
skills.key: Theoretical: what should happen (favorable/total). Experimental: what did happen (occurrences/trials). Prediction = P x number of trials. More trials brings them closer.
tiers: experimental P from a frequency table
predicted count from theoretical P and n trials
compare experimental to theoretical; explain a discrepancy
build a non-uniform model from data (paper cup lands open-end down)
skills.gen: Trials 20..600; frequencies summing to trials; theoretical from spinners/dice.

errors.desc: expects experiment to equal theory exactly
reports P instead of P x n

skills.skin: 600 missile launches vs expected duds, radar hit logs, ejection seat test data

skills.name: Measures of center
skills.key: Mean = sum / count. Median = middle value AFTER sorting (average the two middles if the count is even). Mode = most frequent. An outlier pulls the mean, not the median.
tiers: mean, median, mode of 5-7 whole numbers
even count (median averages two); a mode of 'none'
effect of an outlier on mean vs median
find a missing value given the mean
skills.gen: Sets of 5-10 values in [0,60]; T3 add one value 3x the max.
skills.skin: sortie times, lock times across missions, kills per pilot

skills.name: Measures of variation
skills.key: Range = max - min. Sort, split at the median, Q1 and Q3 are the medians of each half. IQR = Q3 - Q1 (the middle 50%).
tiers: range of a data set
Q1, Q3, IQR for 7-9 values
IQR with even counts; mean absolute deviation (MAD) for 5-6 values
compare spreads of two squadrons
skills.gen: Values in [0,100]; T2 odd counts; T3 even counts.

errors.desc: includes the median in both halves on odd counts

skills.skin: consistency of landing times, spread of fuel burn across a squadron

skills.name: Choosing appropriate measures
skills.key: Symmetric data with no outliers: use mean and MAD. Skewed data or outliers: use median and IQR.
tiers: symmetric vs skewed from a dot plot
pick the best measure of center and say why
how an outlier changes which measure to use
compare two distributions and justify the choice
skills.gen: Generate dot plots: symmetric (mirror), left/right skew, one outlier.
skills.skin: sortie durations with one aborted mission, kill counts across pilots

skills.name: Box-and-whisker plots
skills.key: Five numbers: min, Q1, median, Q3, max. The box is the middle 50%. Each of the four sections holds about a quarter of the data no matter how long it looks.
tiers: read min/Q1/median/Q3/max off a plot
build the five-number summary from data
what percent of data is above Q1 / inside the box
compare two box plots (center and spread)
skills.gen: Data 9-15 values in [0,100]; plots on a 0-100 axis.

errors.desc: box holds half the VALUES not half the DATA

skills.skin: two squadrons' sortie times side by side, lock-time distributions

skills.name: Samples and populations
skills.key: A sample must be random and representative to support a valid inference. A convenience sample (just the pilots in the ready room) is biased.
tiers: population vs sample identification
random vs biased sampling method
which sample best represents the population; why
design a fair sampling method for a base-wide survey
skills.gen: Scenario templates with 3-4 sampling methods, exactly one random.

errors.desc: a large sample must be fair

skills.skin: surveying pilots about a new helmet, maintenance inspections across bases

skills.name: Using random samples to describe populations
skills.key: Estimate for the population = sample proportion x population size. Different samples give different estimates; that variation is expected.
tiers: proportion in sample -> estimate for population
estimate a population mean from a sample
compare estimates from several samples; give a reasonable range
judge whether a sample size is large enough
skills.gen: Sample 20-100, population 500-5000; proportions with clean fractions.

errors.desc: reports the sample count as the estimate

skills.skin: estimate how many of 2,400 missiles are duds from a sample of 60

skills.name: Comparing populations
skills.key: Compare centers (mean or median) AND spreads. Divide the difference in centers by the MAD to see how big the difference really is.
tiers: which group has the higher center
difference in means expressed in MADs
overlap: similar spreads, different centers
write a comparison statement using both center and spread
skills.gen: Two sets of 8-12 values; MAD chosen so difference/MAD lands in {0.5,1,2,3}.

errors.desc: reports the MAD as the difference

skills.skin: Eagle squadron vs Falcon squadron sortie times

skills.name: Using random samples to compare populations
skills.key: Use samples from each population, compare centers and spreads, and say how confident you are: overlapping boxes mean a weak conclusion.
tiers: read two sample box plots and compare medians
compare using mean and range
decide whether the difference is meaningful given the spread
recommend more sampling or a conclusion
skills.gen: Two samples 10-15 values each; vary overlap.
skills.skin: do F-16 pilots or F-15 pilots lock faster? sampled from two bases
